name: Disappointment Peak Cleaver (Gerdine Ridge / Cool Glacier)

pitch_detail.notes: Contour below Glacier Gap Peak, then regain the ridge.
NE traverse around 8,400 ft; rockfall-exposed below Disappointment Peak.
Ascend westward, regain the ridge at the glacier's top.

descent_text: No rappelling; reverse the ascent line on foot. From the summit, descend the ridge to the 9,600 ft col, then down the Cool Glacier to the 9,100 ft col. On the traverse back beneath Disappointment Peak, keep lower and farther from the face than on the way in to cut the time spent under its rockfall. Crevasses on the Cool Glacier open wider as summer goes on and snow bridges weaken, so stay roped and probe suspect bridges. From Glacier Gap, return across the White Chuck basin to White Pass and out the North Fork Sauk River Trail.
approach: From the North Fork Sauk River Trailhead (2,050 ft, off FR 49/Sloan Creek Road), hike ~9 mi to White Pass on the PCT. Continue east on the Foam Creek Trail ~2 mi, cross a ridge saddle near 6,600 ft, then traverse the White Chuck Glacier basin trending NE to Glacier Gap (~7,300 ft), the standard high camp where the Suiattle and White Chuck glaciers meet. Summit day is roughly 7 mi round trip with about 3,450 ft of gain, some of it height lost and regained along the way: climb gentle snow above camp, follow a climber's track on volcanic scree onto the Gerdine and Cool glaciers, end-run a crevasse or two, then rejoin the climber's trail for the final steep pitch to the summit.
overview: The Gerdine Ridge and Cool Glacier route climbs Glacier Peak's south side, typically via the White Pass and Glacier Gap. It is a popular alternative to the Sitkum, often combined with a scenic high traverse beneath the peak.
beta: From Glacier Gap (7,300 ft), ascend northward, initially contouring the left slope below Glacier Gap Peak (7,739 ft), then regain the ridge and continue to about 8,400 ft. Traverse NE onto the upper Suiattle Glacier, then ascend the Cool Glacier westward until regaining the ridge at its top, finishing to the summit. A variant stays on the nose of the cleaver where the standard line steps onto the glacier near 8,500-8,600 ft, following a climbers' path when melted out up mostly Class 3-4 ground with a few low fifth-class moves over Disappointment Peak (9,755 ft), then drops about 150 ft to the saddle above the Cool Glacier to rejoin the standard route. It avoids most of the glacier travel and crevasse hazard in exchange for sustained loose, rockfall-prone scrambling.
gear: Rope for glacier travel — the route crosses numerous ice bridges over deep crevasses on both the Gerdine and Cool Glaciers
Full crevasse rescue kit (pickets, prusik cords or mechanical ascenders, pulley, extra lockers)
1-2 snow pickets for anchors/belays on steeper glacier sections
Helmet — icefall exposure while crossing the glaciers
No rock gear needed — the final pumice/rock ridge to the summit is unroped class 2-3
fa: Thomas Gerdine, Sam Strom, A. H. Dubor, and Darcy Bard (USGS survey party), 1897 — the mountain's first ascent; the party initially summited a sub-peak in fog (later named Disappointment Peak) before completing the true summit.
